name: Diffusion of an Ink Drop in Water
subject: chemistry
ncert_reference: NCERT textbook portal; Class 9 matter chapter page to verify
educational_goal: Observe diffusion and relate the spreading of particles to temperature and particle motion.
safety_notes: Use warm water that is safe to handle, not boiling water.
Keep liquids away from electrical equipment.

gaps: The supplied Class XII chemistry units do not specify this record's complete procedure and doses; original values are unchanged.
quantity_review.policy: Ranges, approximations, stock amounts, final volumes, capacities, ratios and endpoint additions retain their distinct meanings. Unstated amounts remain absent. Transcription is not scientific approval.

procedure_steps.instruction: Fill one beaker with cold water and one with warm water.
procedure_steps.observation: The two beakers contain equal-looking water at different temperatures.

procedure_steps.instruction: Place one drop of ink gently in the center of each beaker without stirring.
procedure_steps.observation: A dark ink region appears at the point of addition.

procedure_steps.instruction: Observe both beakers for the same time interval.
procedure_steps.observation: Ink spreads through warm water faster than through cold water.

procedure_steps.instruction: Record the relative diffusion rates and explain the observation using particle motion.
procedure_steps.observation: Higher temperature is associated with faster visible spreading.
